intro: Clothes that fit or do not, what happens to them in the wash, and the vocabulary of paying and complaining.
b1.texto:
**How it fits.** **Quedar** + adjective, like gustar: **me queda apretado** (tight), **flojo** (loose), **ajustado**, **amplio**, **largo**, **corto**. **Me aprietan** los zapatos. **Me sienta bien** means it suits me.

**What happens to clothes.** **Encoger** (to shrink): **ha encogido** en la lavadora. **Dar de sí** (to stretch): el jersey **ha dado de sí**. **Desteñir** (to run). **Arrugarse**. A seam **se descose**, and you **coses** it with **aguja** and **hilo**. A coat goes **al tinte** to be cleaned **en seco**.

**Parts.** **La cremallera**, **los botones**, **el bolsillo**, **la manga**, **el cuello**. In the shop: **la percha**, **la etiqueta**, **el probador**.

**Kinds.** **Ropa de temporada**, **de abrigo**, **de cama**. **Liso** or **estampado**, **de rayas**, **de cuadros**. **Está de moda**, **está pasado de moda**.

**In the shop.** **Solo estoy echando un vistazo.** **¿Quién da la vez?** (who is last in the queue?)

**Paying.** **Al contado** (all at once) or **a plazos** (in instalments), **con tarjeta** or **en efectivo**. To reserve something you **dejas una señal**. You ask for **la factura** or **el recibo**, and before a big job, **un presupuesto**.

**Complaining.** Every Spanish business must have **hojas de reclamaciones**. You **pides la hoja de reclamaciones** and **pones una reclamación**. **El consumidor** has rights: **la garantía**, **la devolución**, **el cambio**.
b2.f0: Good morning. I bought this jacket a week ago and, on washing it, it has shrunk two sizes.
b2.f1: Did you wash it at home? The label says it has to be taken to the dry cleaner's.
b2.f2: The label had come unstitched and I didn't see it. Besides, the zip was already broken when I got it.
b2.f3: I'm sorry. If you have the invoice, I can exchange it for another one, but not give you your money back.
b2.f4: I paid for it in cash and here is the receipt. I would prefer you to give me my money back.
b2.f5: That is not up to me. If you like, I'll bring you the complaints form.
b4.pregunta: Complete: these trousers are tight on me.
b5.pregunta: The jumper is bigger after washing. It…
b6.pregunta: You pay a little every month. You pay…
b6.o0.refuerzo: A plazos means in instalments, paying a little each month.
b7.o1.explicacion: Echar un vistazo: to have a look.
b7.o2.explicacion: Echar un vistazo: to have a look.
b8.pregunta: Complete: I would prefer you to change it for me.
b8.o0.refuerzo: Preferiría que takes the imperfect subjunctive, so cambiaran fits.
b8.o2.refuerzo: The clause after que needs the subjunctive.
b9.pregunta: To reserve a sofa until next week, the shop asks you to…
b9.o1.refuerzo: That is to ask for a quote.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That is to say who is last in a queue.
b10.traduccion: I want to make a complaint about this product.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a formal complaint on a complaints form about a faulty product and a shop that refuses to refund you.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Argue aloud with a shop assistant who will not accept a return, firmly but politely.
b7.o0.explicacion: Solo estoy echando un vistazo means I'm just having a look around.
